response.sql: WITH pat AS (SELECT p.ID, p.SEX, AVG(l.ALB) - AVG(l.TP) AS alb_tp, AVG(l.APTT - l.PT) AS aptt_pt FROM Patient p JOIN Laboratory l ON l.ID = p.ID GROUP BY p.ID, p.SEX), sx AS (SELECT SEX, AVG(alb_tp) AS alb_tp, AVG(aptt_pt) AS aptt_pt FROM pat GROUP BY SEX), m AS (SELECT AVG(aptt_pt) AS mean_ap FROM sx) SELECT AVG(sx.alb_tp) AS avg_alb_minus_tp, AVG(sx.aptt_pt) AS avg_aptt_minus_pt, AVG(sx.aptt_pt) - (SELECT mean_ap FROM m) AS exceed_mean FROM sx WHERE sx.aptt_pt > (SELECT mean_ap FROM m)

assumptions.assumption: The per-patient ALB−TP figure is AVG(ALB) − AVG(TP), each over that patient's own non-missing values. The per-patient APTT−PT figure is the average of per-row differences, so only rows with both APTT and PT present count.
The inner join drops lab records with no matching patient, and also drops patients with no lab records. SEX values of NULL, blank or any other value each form their own group.

The mean for the threshold is the unweighted average of the sex-level APTT−PT averages across all sexes, including those that are later filtered out. The excess is the average of the kept sexes' APTT−PT figures minus that mean. If no sex passes the filter, the query returns a row of NULLs.
